There is no single universal date when it became illegal to smoke indoors, as bans were introduced at different times in different jurisdictions. According to the BBC and WHO, Ireland was the first country to pass a national smoke-free law in 2004, banning smoking in workplaces, restaurants, and bars [d7]. In the UK, smoking was banned in virtually all indoor places in Scotland in 2006 and in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland in July 2007 [d9]. In the United States, Delaware was the first state to implement a comprehensive smoke-free law in 2002, followed by New York in 2003 and Massachusetts in 2004, while San Luis Obispo, California adopted the first US law eliminating smoking in bars as early as 1990 [d4]. At the federal level, President Clinton banned smoking in US federal government buildings by executive order in 1997 [d8]. Globally, by 2023 around 71% of the world's population was covered by at least one smoke-free policy [d7], reflecting a gradual, jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction process rather than a single worldwide ban date.
